zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is directly left/right of Y (or that X and Y are next to each other), enforce that the house numbers differ by exactly one and respect the direction (X = Y-1 for left, X = Y+1 for right).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains phrases like “directly left of”, “directly right of”, “next to”, “immediately to the …”.
zebralogic.example: Placing Peter two houses away from Eric despite the clue “Peter is directly left of Eric”.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is somewhere to the left/right of Y, enforce a strict ordering (X < Y for left, X > Y for right) without assuming adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues containing “somewhere to the left of”, “to the right of”, “to the left of”, “to the right of”.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the Chinese nationality left of the Dane even though the clue required the Chinese to be to the right of the Dane.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., “The British is the person who owns a Honda Civic”), bind those values to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues that use “is the”, “equals”, “the same as”, “is the … of”.
zebralogic.example: Treating “British = Honda Civic” as a loose hint and placing the British and the Honda Civic in different houses.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., “The cat is in the second house”), assign that attribute directly to that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues that mention a house number explicitly.
zebralogic.example: Putting the cat in house 3 despite the clue “The cat is in the second house”.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with no extra text after it, to guarantee the verifier extracts the answer correctly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the end of every solution generation.
zebralogic.example: Appending explanatory sentences after the JSON, causing the verifier to miss the solution.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between X and Y, enforce that the absolute difference in house numbers equals N + 1 (i.e., exactly N houses in between).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues containing “N houses between”, “one house between”, “two houses between”.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting “one house between” as “adjacent” and putting the two items next to each other.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from being in a particular house (e.g., “The mystery book is not in house 6”), ensure that assignment never occurs.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues with “not in house X”, “cannot be”, “does not live in”.
zebralogic.example: Placing the mystery genre in house 6 despite the clue prohibiting it.

zebralogic.title: CanonicalCaseMatching
zebralogic.principle: Output attribute values with the exact capitalization as given in the problem statement; do not alter case.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing any value into the final JSON.
zebralogic.example: Writing “Fish” and “Mountain” instead of the required “fish” and “mountain”.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalencePropagation
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (e.g., A = B and B = C), deduce the direct equivalence A = C and propagate it throughout the grid.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever two or more equivalence clues share a common attribute value.
zebralogic.example: Linking “British = Honda Civic” and “Honda Civic = British” but failing to propagate that the British also owns the other attributes tied to the Honda Civic, leading to inconsistency.

zebralogic.title: ExactAttributeValueMatching
zebralogic.principle: Always copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem’s attribute list; never substitute synonyms, alternate spellings, or morphological variants.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When filling any cell of the solution grid.
zebralogic.example: Using “swedish” for the nationality instead of the listed value “swede”.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart'
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the meaning of ‘between’, assuming the count includes the endpoints.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that ‘N houses between’ means there are exactly N houses separating X and Y, so the house numbers differ by N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model adds explanations or formatting after the JSON, not realizing the verifier stops parsing at the first JSON block.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Print the JSON as the very last output, with no trailing characters.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the final answer to be truncated
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model adds too much reasoning or verbose output before the JSON.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise and place the JSON at the end; if needed, summarize constraints briefly.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats negative clues as optional hints rather than hard constraints.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat any ‘not in house X’ statement as a hard prohibition and exclude that house from the candidate set.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model defaults to title case when generating text.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy the attribute values verbatim, preserving the case shown in the problem.

zebralogic.description: Failing to propagate transitive equivalence across multiple clues, leading to inconsistent assignments
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model handles each equivalence in isolation.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After processing each equivalence, propagate the relation through all linked attributes before assigning houses.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model forgets to output the final grid or thinks the answer is already given.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with a correctly formatted JSON block containing the full solution.

zebralogic.description: Using non-canonical attribute values (synonyms) instead of the exact values from the list
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to be natural‑language friendly and replaces the listed term with a more common word.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values exactly from the provided list; never invent or modify them.
